body: I used the above headline because this movie is good but could have been great with a better plot. Not saying that this plot is not good its just kinda weak because by the end it kinda makes is predictable and obvious. Maybe because it is based on real life incident, maybe because of plot idk..the point is this movie has everything from a soldiers love for his country, a love for his family (loved ones), it properly shows what problems our soldiers faced during those era also some face until today. In 2025 it's kinda difficult to find a movie in Bollywood which keeps you attracted almost entire times without any nudity, item song or adult scenes. They completely respected a soldiers personal life and kept it away from screen in public which is a pretty good thing to do...Mad respect to all the soldiers who sacrificed for us in past and also who are standing tall today between us and our enemies. I'll recomend to give this movie a chance, maybe a one time watch for many of you but still this effort should not go in vain...Just if plot could have been stronger we could have gotten a masterpeice today.

Sky Force is based on an incident that happened during India's first airstrike on Pakistan in 1965 that a very few people know, atleast I didn't.

Without a doubt, everyone should watch this film. Also, it's a sincere, to the point, no nonsense film. The story is about Veer Pahariya's character while Akshay Kumar is the group captain who investigates what happened with him.

The actors are all good, Akshay as the lead is superb, Sharad Kelkar also has an important part, Veer is decent, Nimrat is crisp, Sara is a little off.

The scenes of the airstrike and the drills have been shot really well. The songs are decent, nothing dramatic.

The only part that doesn't work for me are the emotional scenes. I didn't feel much connected, especially with Sara in them.

Overall, this is a real story that is worth knowing about. In a chaos of mass entertainers that solely depend on stars and spice, this film stands on its story and is a must watch!!

Sky Force has the structure of a powerful, emotionally charged war drama, but it falters in its execution, making it a truly missed opportunity. 6.5/10

The core story - Akshay Kumar's commander fighting bureaucracy years later to honor his missing pilot's sacrifice - is genuinely compelling and refreshingly avoids the typical jingoism. I appreciated that this was a war film about duty and justice, not just fighting.

However, the film stumbles badly on two crucial fronts. First, the special effects, especially during the climactic air combat sequences, are often distractingly tacky. In the post-Top Gun: Maverick era, the low-budget feel of the plane visuals pulls you right out of the action, despite the well-choreographed dogfights.

Second, and more damagingly, the casting of the pivotal pilot 'Tabby' is a misfire. The character is written as the film's emotional heart, yet the debutant actor delivers a one-dimensional, expressionless performance that prevents any audience attachment. When the narrative calls for palpable anguish, the character offers a blank stare. This single performance flaw undercuts the entire emotional payoff of the second half.

An avoidable, early song also breaks the momentum before the war even begins. A solid effort, but a few critical, avoidable missteps keep this flight grounded.
